items.descZh: 该产品是一个免费的在线随机单词生成器，旨在为用户提供快速生成随机单词的服务，适用于语言学习、游戏和创意写作。核心功能包括按词性（如名词、动词、形容词）、首字母、尾字母、长度和音节数进行精确过滤，并支持点击复制和批量收集单词到面板。亮点在于其强大的过滤系统，支持多达15种语言，例如可以生成特定长度如4字母或11字母的单词，以及特定音节数如1音节或4音节的单词，确保高度定制化。适用场景广泛，包括派对游戏、单词游戏、拼图和交叉字谜等需要随机单词的活动。

items.title: Show HN: Watch a neural net learn Clash Royale defense in the browser
items.desc: description: Watch a small neural network learn to defend a tower in seconds, scored by a real Clash Royale simulator compiled to WebAssembly and running in your browser. MatchupChange Matchup Attacker Your defender No defence \ Random drop \ Best possible \ Measured by trying every cell and every delay on the five attacks below. Train Show me See results Drag onto the board Skip demo 1. 1Your turn 2. 2AI's turn 3. 3Results Defend it yourself Five attacks. Drag your card onto the board to drop it, where and when you like. Each round scores the share of tower damage you prevented. Start round 1 Skip to the AI Watch it learn It starts knowing nothing. Each try, the engine drops the attacker somewhere new, the network picks a cell and a moment, and the engine reports the damage. Train Reset Watch Full speed Tries0 Per second0 Time0.0s Drag the red attacker on the board: the heatmap shows where the network would drop your defender. Show me See results Same five attacks You The learner Keep training Try another matchup Finish Damage prevented on the five attacks An interactive demo Can you outthink a neural network that has never seen the game? 1. 1 Pick a matchup. An enemy attack heads for your tower. You get one defending card. 2. 2 Defend it yourself. Drag the card onto the board. Where you drop it and when both count. Optional. 3. 3 Watch a network learn it. It starts from zero. A real Clash Royale simulator, written in C++ and compiled to WebAssembly, scores every try right here in your browser. Start Takes about two minutes, with a tensecond howtoplay demo first if you want one. Works with a mouse or a finger. How it works The engine. The arena, the troops, the towers and every hit are simulated by the project's C++ engine, the same code the full agent trains against, compiled to WebAssembly. It is deterministic: the same drop always gives the same result. The problem. The attacker is dropped at a random spot on the enemy side (a Goblin Barrel is thrown at a random spot around one of your towers). The network chooses a legal cell for your defender, then a delay from 0 to 5 seconds. The reward is the share of the nodefence tower damage it prevented. Your defender's health counts only as a tiebreaker: of two drops that save exactly as much of the tower, it prefers the one that keeps its card alive, and it never gives up a single tower hit point to do so. The score on the page is the damage prevented alone, for you and for it. The network. A few thousand weights in plain JavaScript, no ML library: the attacker's position goes in, a map of cell preferences and a delay choice come out. It learns with REINFORCE, the simplest policygradient method: tries that beat the usual result for that spawn become more likely. The honest part. This is a miniature. The real agent picks from a hand of four cards with an elixir economy, every second of a threeminute match, and needs days of training. Close × Game over Game over What you just played is a small corner of ClashRoyaleAi, an opensource project to teach a neural network to play Clash Royale. The engine. A Clash Royale battle simulator written in C++, with more than a hundred cards, played out tick by tick. The same code scored every try on this page, compiled to WebAssembly. The agent. A network with a convolutional eye and a recurrent memory, trained with PPO, that plays whole threeminute matches: a hand of four cards, an elixir bar, every second a decision. It learns against scripted teachers first, then against past versions of itself. The hardware. One laptop CPU, no GPU. A training run takes days. [See the project on GitHub](https://github.com/itzik123/ClashRoyaleAi) Try another matchup If you enjoyed it, a star on GitHub helps other people find it.

items.descZh: 该产品是一个基于Web的交互式演示，源自开源项目ClashRoyaleAi，旨在通过实时模拟展示神经网络在《皇室战争》中学习防御塔的机制。核心功能允许用户选择对战，手动放置防御卡或观看AI从零开始学习，通过尝试不同放置位置和延迟来优化策略。亮点包括使用编译为WebAssembly的C++引擎进行确定性评分，确保高性能；神经网络仅由几千个权重组成，采用REINFORCE算法学习，奖励基于防止的塔伤害份额，演示整体约需两分钟。适用场景涵盖对人工智能、游戏策略或教育演示感兴趣的用户，可作为互动学习工具。

items.title: Show HN: Lines of C, Beats QOI
items.desc: Hi. I made tinycodec. A lossless image codec that, on aggregate from my 3,167 image corpus, beat QOI on encoding speed, decoding speed, and file size. There's also an available readable version, which is 164 lines of C code, the golfed version being 45. Apache-2.0.
items.author: ozzymitchell
items.descZh: tinycodec 是一款新兴的无损图像编解码器，旨在提供超越现有方案的综合性能。其核心功能是实现高效的无损图像压缩与解压，并提供了可读版和极致精简的 golfed 版本两种 C 语言实现。主要亮点在于，在包含 3167 张图片的测试语料库中，它在编码速度、解码速度和文件体积三个维度上均超越了知名的 QOI 格式。可读版仅需 164 行代码，而 golfed 版更是压缩至 45 行，体现了极高的代码简洁性。该编解码器采用 Apache-2.0 开源许可，适用于对编码效率、运行速度和存储空间有严苛要求的图像处理场景。
items.quote: 一种无损图像编解码器，在我 3,167 张图片的语料库中，其编码速度、解码速度和文件大小均优于 QOI。

items.author: vpbhardwaj
items.descZh: SuperLocalMemory 4.0 是一个面向 AI Agent 的本地优先受治理内存操作系统，旨在统一多通道检索与强审计控制。其核心功能包括 reciprocal rank fusion 多通道检索、双时态召回、多范围隔离、基于角色的访问控制及哈希链审计追踪，由生成围栏准入和可验证事务等可靠性主干支撑。在 11 个故障注入场景各重复 200 次的测试中，系统维护了 2199 个 scoped component properties，展现出高可靠性。性能方面，受治理写入耗时 11.0 ms，其中包络开销占 70.6%，但生成围栏仅 1.9 微秒、义务账本 42 微秒，说明成本源于持久性而非治理本身。该系统特别适用于对记忆一致性、安全审计和故障恢复有严格要求的 AI Agent 应用场景。
items.quote: 对包络进行适当的定时给出了11.0 ms的受控写入，其中包络是70.6%，但是生成栅栏花费1.9微秒，并且所需的时间是1.0 ms。
items.titleZh: 展示HN：SuperLocalMemory 4.0“用于AI代理的受控内存操作系统”

This is created for the purpose of learning about VMs, disassemblers and property based testing. Inspired by Justin Meiners and Ryan Pendleton's [Write Your Own VM](https://www.jmeiners.com/lc3vm/). [](/shraddhaag/toyvm/blob/main/rogue.gif) To test out the LC3 instruction implementation, I am using 2 kind of tests: 1. Property based tests which makes use of [Hegel](https://hegel.dev/)'s library for Golang, [hegelgo](https://github.com/hegeldev/hegelgo), found in [instructions\_property\_test.go](/shraddhaag/toyvm/blob/main/instructions%5Fproperty%5Ftest.go). 2. Traditional example based tests, found in [instructions\_test.go](/shraddhaag/toyvm/blob/main/instructions%5Ftest.go)Inspired by Justin Meiners and Ryan Pendleton's [Write Your Own VM](https://www.jmeiners.com/lc3vm/). Emulator Before implementing the VM itself, I wanted to understand: 1. What is the disassembled output for an LC3 compatible object file. 2. What does the changing registers and memory look like? Initially I implemented a [disassembler](/shraddhaag/toyvm/blob/main/disassembler). Later, I converted it into a full blown emulator You can try it out here: [lc3.shraddhaag.dev](https://lc3.shraddhaag.dev). Usage of LLMs The VM is written entirely by hand. The tests (both table based tests and property based tests) and the emulator are written with the aid of LLMs. About A toy VM created for learning for the LC3 computer. items.desc: description: Answer customer questions and book appointments from your own website, app or AI agent. title: CallChatSyn — Voice & Message Agents for Business image: https://callchatsyn.com/ogimage.png CallChatSyn API Use your business's CallChatSyn answering bot and booking calendar from your own website, app or AI agent. Same answers your customers get on WhatsApp and your booking page. Machinereadable spec: [openapi.json](/openapi.json). Founder offer: free for the first 1,000 businesses Answering bot, order status and bookings through the API on any plan, with no trial expiry (up to 100 API calls a day, 2,000 a month). Building for clients? Each client business claims its own spot. 1. Create a free account and confirm your email. 2. Add your FAQs and opening hours (2 minutes). 3. Open Dashboard → Developers, click _Claim founder API access_, and create a key. [Start free and claim a founder spot](/signup?plan=lite%5Fplus&utm%5Fsource=apipage)[I already have an account](/dashboard/developers) Try it now, no signup Use the public demo key ccs_demo_public with any example below. It answers as our demo business, and bookings are dry runs: you see the time would be booked, but nothing is saved. It's shared by everyone, so it allows 500 calls a day in total. curl https://callchatsyn.com/api/v1/answer \ H "Authorization: Bearer ccs_demo_public" \ H "ContentType: application/json" \ d '{"message": "Where are you located?"}' 1\. Get a key In [Dashboard → Developers](/dashboard/developers), create a key. It's shown once; keep it on your server, never in browser code. Send it on every request as Authorization: Bearer ccs_live_…. 2\. Answer a customer's message curl https://callchatsyn.com/api/v1/answer \ H "Authorization: Bearer $CCS_KEY" \ H "ContentType: application/json" \ d '{"message": "What are your opening hours?"}' {"intent":"faq","lang":"en","matched":true,"reply":"We're open every day, 9am to 9pm."} 3\. Book an appointment curl https://callchatsyn.com/api/v1/slots H "Authorization: Bearer $CCS_KEY" {"slots":[{"start":"20261010T02:00:00.000Z","label":"Sat 10 Oct, 10:00"}],"services":["Haircut"],"locations":["Main St"]} curl https://callchatsyn.com/api/v1/bookings \ H "Authorization: Bearer $CCS_KEY" H "ContentType: application/json" \ d '{"start":"20261010T02:00:00.000Z","service":"Haircut","name":"Ana","email":"ana@example.com"}' 201 {"booked":true,"start":"20261010T02:00:00.000Z","label":"Sat 10 Oct, 10:00"} Use it from an AI assistant (MCP) The opensource [callchatsynmcp](https://github.com/oneappsworld/callchatsynmcp) server gives Claude, Cursor and other MCP clients three tools: answer a customer question, list open times, book an appointment. { "mcpServers": { "callchatsyn": { "command": "npx", "args": ["y", "github:oneappsworld/callchatsynmcp"], "env": { "CALLCHATSYN_API_KEY": "ccs_live_..." } } } } Errors and limits Errors look like {"error":{"code":"…","message":"…"}}. With the demo key, POST /api/v1/bookings returns 200 with {"booked":false,"demo":true} instead of booking. 401 bad key · 402 plan inactive · 403 feature not in plan · 429 usage limit · 400/404/409 request problems. Each request counts toward the business's plan limits, the same as WhatsApp and bookingpage messages. The answering bot, order status and bookings are included on the Pro plan. Founder offer: the first 1,000 businesses to claim it in Dashboard → Developers get them free on any plan (up to 100 API calls a day, 2,000 a month).

items.title: Show HN: jpm – a JavaScript package manager in Rust, every line by Claude Code
items.desc: description: jpm installs npm packages fast, from one ~2 MB binary, with dependencies' install scripts off and new versions held back a day by default. A dropin for npm, pnpm, yarn and bun projects. title: jpm: a fast, small, securebydefault package manager for JavaScript image: https://getjpm.sh/og.png [Skip to content](main) jpm A fast, small, securebydefault package manager for JavaScript macOS / LinuxWindows $ curl fsSL https://getjpm.sh shCopy irm https://getjpm.sh/install.ps1 iexCopy [Get started](start)[GitHub](https://github.com/jtwebman/jpm) Every line written by Claude Code. Directed by one engineer. Checked against everyone else's tests. \~2 MBone binary, no runtime to install 1.22 scold nuxt install on GitHub CI 34 MBmemory used to install nuxt on GitHub CI Speed Fast where your CI spends its time Three real projects, four install phases, eight package managers, against the live npm registry. On GitHub CI jpm is the fastest in 9 of 12 cells; the other three are shown as measured. Machine GitHub CI, LinuxmacOS, M4 MaxWindows 11 Phase coldwarmcirepeat Project nitronuxtnext No cache, no lockfile, no node\_modules. Repeat installs were not measured on Windows. Install wall time, shorter is fasterGitHub CI, Linux · nuxt · 591 packages 1. jpm1.22 s 2. bun1.28 s 3. pnpm1.72 s 4. aube3.00 s 5. upm3.52 s 6. deno7.64 s 7. yarn9.63 s 8. npm18.54 s __GitHub CI, Linux, cold, nuxt · 591 packages__ Package manager Wall time jpm 1.22 s bun 1.4.2 1.28 s pnpm 12.8.1 1.72 s aube 2.6.0 3.00 s upm 1.3.1 3.52 s deno 2.9.6 7.64 s yarn 4.18.1 9.63 s npm 12.1.0 18.54 s jpm is the fastest here, 15× faster than npm. Defender scans every file an install writes, and it scans files written by node.exe (npm, upm) far more cheaply than files written by native tools like jpm, aube and pnpm. On Windows jpm is the fastest on next, not yet on nuxt. Wall time, medians: ubuntulatest with 4 cores (5 runs), macOS on an M4 Max (5 runs) and Windows 11 with Defender on (3 runs), 20260930 and 20261001\. Full tables, with CPU time, in [docs/benchmarks.md](https://github.com/jtwebman/jpm/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md). Get started Switch in one command Run jpm install in your project. jpm imports the lockfile you have into its own jpm.lock, with the same versions. packagelock.json and npmshrinkwrap.json (npm 7+), pnpmlock.yaml (pnpm 9+) and bun.lock are carried over as they are: the same versions and the same tree, with no registry lookups. yarn.lock, from yarn 1 or yarn 2 and later, keeps every version yarn picked. jpm asks the registry only for what yarn.lock doesn't record: peers, platforms and bins. Your old lockfile is left untouched. Delete it when you're ready. CI keeps working during the switch: jpm ci and jpm install frozenlockfile install from the old lockfile as it is until jpm.lock is committed. It also reads workspaces, pnpmworkspace.yaml, catalogs, overrides and resolutions, and patches. Older formats, outofdate lockfiles and the rest: [docs/migrating.md](https://github.com/jtwebman/jpm/blob/main/docs/migrating.md). npmpackagelock.json pnpmpnpmlock.yaml yarnyarn.lock bunbun.lock jpmjpm.lock jpmlock 2 package @babel/[email protected] integrity sha512… dep @babel/generator 7.29.8 $ cd yourproject $ jpm install reads packagelock.json / pnpmlock.yaml / yarn.lock / bun.lock → writes jpm.lock Lean Small enough to forget it's there One binary with nothing behind it, an install that holds little in memory, and a store that keeps each file once. Not every number goes jpm's way: npm and yarn keep compressed tarballs, so their caches are smaller. jpm keeps its files unpacked, ready to link. GitHub CI, Linux, 20260930\. Binary sizes are the README's round figures. Binary size, approximate 1. jpm\~2 MB 2. pnpm\~60 MB 3. bun\~80 MB 4. aube\~150 MB __Binary size, approximate__ jpm \~2 MB pnpm \~60 MB bun \~80 MB aube \~150 MB Peak memory, nuxt ci install 1. jpm34 MB 2. bun89 MB 3. pnpm184 MB 4. npm387 MB __Peak memory, nuxt ci install__ jpm 34 MB bun 89 MB pnpm 184 MB npm 387 MB Disk after a cold nuxt install, node\_modules and store 1. jpm244 MB 2. bun261 MB 3. pnpm290 MB 4. npm443 MB __Disk after a cold nuxt install, node\_modules and store__ jpm 244 MB bun 261 MB pnpm 290 MB npm 443 MB CI cache after a cold next install 1. npm194 MB 2. yarn328 MB 3. jpm347 MB 4. pnpm433 MB 5. bun466 MB __CI cache after a cold next install__ npm 194 MB yarn 328 MB jpm 347 MB pnpm 433 MB bun 466 MB Storage Each file stored once. Each package built once. jpm keeps one store per machine and builds each package's directory once, for every project that uses it. Installing again is mostly making links. 1. A contentaddressed store Each tarball is checked against its integrity, then unpacked once into ~/.jpm/store. Every file is kept once, by its hash, readonly. 2. A global virtual store Each package is built once as an entry: name@version, plus a short digest of its dependency graph when it has dependencies. Its files are hardlinked from the store, and its dependencies are linked beside it, so it can import only what it declared. 3. Your node\_modules A project's node_modules links to those entries. A warm install makes only these few links: 4 ms for nitro on GitHub CI. 4. Every other project The next project on the machine links to the same entries. When nothing changed, a repeat install checks a few links and is done in 1–2 ms. \~/.jpm/storefiles, by hash3fa19c07e4b271d80b5ec6a3hardlinks\~/.jpm/store/v1/linksentries, built once[\[email protected\]](/cdncgi/l/emailprotection)node\_modules/debugnode\_modules/ms[\[email protected\]](/cdncgi/l/emailprotection)node\_modules/msappone/apptwo/node\_modules/debugnode\_modules/debuglinksPause the animation Next.js and Nuxt: inside the project Next's Turbopack compiles nothing outside the project, and Nuxt imports packages it doesn't declare. items.descZh: jpm 是一款专为追求极致效率与安全性而设计的轻量级 JavaScript 包管理器，旨在作为 npm、pnpm、yarn 和 bun 的即插即用替代品。它采用仅约 2 MB 的单一二进制分发，无需安装运行时，默认禁用依赖安装脚本并延迟新版本发布一天以构建安全防线。在 GitHub CI 的真实测试中，jpm 安装 591 个包仅耗时 1.22 秒，比 npm 快 15 倍，并在 12 项基准测试中的 9 项里夺得速度榜首。其资源控制同样出色，安装 nuxt 时的峰值内存仅 34 MB，磁盘占用 244 MB，且借助内容寻址存储实现了 4 毫秒级的极速热安装。该工具非常适合对安全扫描友好、内存和磁盘空间受限的 CI/CD 流水线、本地开发环境以及大规模 Monorepo 项目。
items.quote: jpm 是这里最快的，比 npm 快 15 倍。
